function.name: telemetry_accept_suggestion
function.description: Turn an alert suggestion telemetry's code analysis drafted into a monitor, optionally overriding its threshold, severity or channels. Without user_approved nothing is written: the answer shows the suggestion and exactly what would be sent. Show it to the user, ask, and call again with `user_approved: true` once they said yes.

user_approved.description: true only after the user said yes to accepting this suggestion in this conversation.

function.name: telemetry_api_get
function.description: Read any other query route of the TaskTrooper Telemetry API when the dedicated telemetry tools do not cover it: hosts, Kubernetes, databases, queues, SLOs (kpis), monitors, web and mobile apps, load tests, profiling. Read-only; it refuses anything that is not a data route. The result is JSON as telemetry returns it.

path.description: The path under the telemetry API root, with no leading /api/v1, for example "infra/hosts", "infra/databases/3/queries", "kpis", "monitors" or "apps/storefront/summary".

query.description: Query parameters as strings, for example {"range": "6h", "env": "production"}.

function.name: telemetry_explain_endpoint
function.description: Why one endpoint got slower or started failing: its own time and each dependency it calls (database, cache, other services) in the window, against a baseline window. The top child that changed is the dependency to blame; a large change in the endpoint's own time points at its own code. No baseline requests means no comparison; retry with baseline 1d or 7d, else say the baseline is missing. Then confirm with telemetry_search_traces on the same endpoint.

baseline.description: What to compare against: prev (the window just before, the default), or 1d / 7d (the same window a day or a week back) when the problem may be older than the window.

endpoint.description: The endpoint: its id slug from telemetry_get_service's endpoints (for example "post-v1-charges"), or "METHOD /route" (for example "POST /v1/charges"), which is looked up for you.

env.description: Deployment environment to read; omit for all.

range.description: The window to explain. It must cover the time the problem started.

service.description: A service name as telemetry reports it (from the incident or telemetry_get_service). Never guess one.

function.name: telemetry_get_incident
function.description: Read one TaskTrooper Telemetry incident with its timeline: when it started, the monitor or SLO that fired, the value and peak, the service and endpoint, the acknowledgement, and the telemetry's own root-cause hint (`rootCause`). That hint is unstructured and only a lead to verify with the other telemetry tools, never a conclusion. This is the monitoring product's incident, not a TaskTrooper incident (those are `get_incident`).

incident_id.description: The telemetry incident id (the "Telemetry incident id" in the task, or an id from telemetry_list_incidents). Never invent one.

function.name: telemetry_get_service
function.description: One service's health in a single call: its error rate, latency and throughput, its endpoints ranked with their ids, its recent deploys and its dependencies. Start here for any service, then go narrower: telemetry_explain_endpoint for why one endpoint got worse, then traces, logs and errors.

env.description: Deployment environment to read; omit for all.

range.description: How far back to look. It must cover the time the problem started or an empty result looks like health.

service.description: A service name as telemetry reports it (it is in the incident). Never guess one.

function.name: telemetry_list_deploys
function.description: List the deploys telemetry saw (a version first seen in spans, or a marker written by CI or the host), newest first. A deploy shortly before an incident started is a correlation worth checking, not proof; say so when you cite it.

env.description: Deployment environment to read; omit for all.

range.description: How far back to look; widen it beyond the incident start.

service.description: A service name as telemetry reports it.

function.name: telemetry_list_errors
function.description: List the error groups telemetry fingerprinted, or read one with its stack. A group whose `firstSeen` sits just after a deploy is a new error from that deploy; one that predates it is background noise to name as such, not to blame on the deploy.

env.description: Deployment environment to read; omit for all.

fingerprint.description: Read this one error group with the stack of its latest occurrence (symbolicated where possible). Give it alone with range.

range.description: How far back to look; it must cover the incident.

service.description: A service name as telemetry reports it.

function.name: telemetry_list_incidents
function.description: List TaskTrooper Telemetry incidents, newest first. Use it to see whether the service had earlier incidents (a recurring one means the previous fix did not hold) and what else is alerting alongside the one you were handed.

endpoint.description: An endpoint in the form "METHOD /route" (for example "POST /v1/orders"), or a consumer process name. The route form, not the endpoint id slug: the wrong form returns an empty list, which is not the same as healthy.

service.description: A service name exactly as telemetry_get_service or the incident reports it.

since.description: Only incidents that started at or after this time, epoch milliseconds.

state.description: Omit it to see everything (a pending incident, one that crossed its threshold but has not fired yet, is often the live problem). open means not resolved.

function.name: telemetry_list_load_tests
function.description: Load tests: the recent runs with their state and result, the scenarios (target, steps, peak load, duration, state draft or ready) and the target domains with whether each is verified. A run only reaches a verified domain, so check here before proposing one, and poll one run by run_id while it is going. Read-only.

run_id.description: Read this one run: state, live VUs, RPS, p95 and error rate while it runs, and the per-step summary and thresholds when it ends. Give it alone.

scenario_id.description: Only the runs of this scenario.

function.name: telemetry_list_monitors
function.description: The monitors (alert rules) telemetry evaluates, each with its kind, target, condition, severity, channels, state and `source` (agent for the ones an agent created; only those may be replaced by an agent), plus the alert suggestions its code analysis drafted. Read it before proposing a monitor so you do not duplicate one, and take channel targets and suggestion ids from here. Read-only.

endpoint.description: Only the monitors of this endpoint, in the form "METHOD /route".

kind.description: Only monitors of this kind, for example latency or error_rate.

service.description: Only the monitors of this service.

suggestions.description: Alert suggestions from telemetry's code analysis to include: proposed (the default), all, or none.

function.name: telemetry_list_slos
function.description: The SLOs (telemetry calls them KPIs): each one's objective, its current SLI, how much error budget is left and the burn rates of its alert rules. Read it before proposing an SLO, so you do not propose one that exists, and to answer "is this service meeting its objectives". Read-only.

service.description: Only the SLOs of this service (or web/mobile app) name.

slo_id.description: Read this one SLO in full. Give it alone.

function.name: telemetry_propose_monitor
function.description: Propose a monitor (an alert rule) in the connected telemetry. Without user_approved nothing is written: the answer replays the monitor over past data (`preview`: how often it would have fired and whether it fires now) and shows exactly what would be sent. Check telemetry_list_monitors first so you do not duplicate one; a monitor that would have fired 0 times on a noisy metric, or many times a day, has the wrong threshold, so fix it and preview again. Then show the user the monitor and its preview, ask, and call again with `user_approved: true` once they said yes. It is created with source agent.

monitor.description: The monitor as telemetry takes it.

channels.description: Notification targets copied from an existing monitor; an empty list opens incidents without notifying.

condition.description: When it fires. Rates are fractions (2% = 0.02), latency is in ms.

forMin.description: Minutes the condition must hold before it fires; 5 is a good default.

minRequests.description: Skip windows with fewer requests, so two requests cannot page anyone.

window.description: The window the value is measured over (default 5m, anomaly 15m).

kind.description: What it watches. latency, error_rate, throughput and apdex need target.service (and target.endpoint for one endpoint); the others are rarer, copy their query shape from an existing monitor.

name.description: A short human name, for example "orders-api p95 latency".

query.description: Kind specific: latency {percentile: p50|p95|p99}; error_rate {statusMin: 500}; throughput {direction: drop|spike|change}; apdex {tMs: 500}; anomaly {metric: error_rate|p95|rpm, direction: up|down|both}; log_count {minSeverity: error, contains?}.

severity.description: critical pages someone; warning and info do not.

status.description: active (the default) or draft, saved but not evaluated.

target.description: service from telemetry, endpoint as "METHOD /route" (omit for the whole service), process for job_missed.

preview_range.description: How much history the preview replays the monitor over; 24h by default, 7d for a rare signal.

replace_id.description: Replace this monitor instead of creating one. Only a monitor an agent created (source agent) can be replaced.

user_approved.description: true only after the user said yes to this exact monitor in this conversation.

function.name: telemetry_propose_slo
function.description: Propose an SLO with burn-rate alerts in the connected telemetry. Without user_approved nothing is written and the answer shows exactly what would be sent. Read telemetry_list_slos first, pick an objective the service meets today (telemetry_get_service), show the user the SLO, ask, and call again with `user_approved: true` once they said yes. It is created with source agent.

replace_id.description: Replace this SLO instead of creating one. Only an SLO an agent created (source agent) can be replaced.

slo.description: The SLO (a telemetry KPI) as telemetry takes it.

alerts.description: Usually two burn-rate rules: fast (longWindow 1h, shortWindow 5m, threshold 14.4, critical) and slow (6h / 30m, 6, warning).

description.description: One sentence: what a good event is and why it matters.

good.description: The good-event rule; thresholdMs is required for a latency SLO.

name.description: The user-facing outcome, for example "Checkout succeeds".

objective.description: The share of good events, between 0 and 1 exclusive, for example 0.99.

owner.description: The team or person who owns it, free text.

sli.description: latency (fast and not a 5xx), availability, or success_rate (not a 5xx).

target.description: kind endpoint, page, journey or app_start; serviceId the service or app name; ref "METHOD /route" for an endpoint, the path for a page.

user_approved.description: true only after the user said yes to this exact SLO in this conversation.

function.name: telemetry_run_load_test
function.description: Run a load test: it sends real traffic to the target. The target must be a domain the user verified in telemetry (Load tests, Domains), and staging is the default. Without user_approved nothing runs: the answer shows the target, the load, the duration and exactly what would be sent. Tell the user those, ask, and call again with `user_approved: true` once they said yes. Then poll telemetry_list_load_tests with the run id every 15 to 30 seconds until it is passed, failed, aborted or error; telemetry_stop_load_test stops it at once.

environment.description: staging (the default) or production. A target that is this repository's production is refused unless this says production, which you pass only when the user explicitly asked to load production.

scenario.description: Or create a new scenario and run it.

spec.description: The scenario spec. Minimal: {target: "https://staging.example.com", mode: "vus", levels: [{name: "warm", ramp: 30, hold: 60, target: 5}, {name: "steady", ramp: 30, hold: 300, target: 20}], steps: ["GET /v1/products", "POST /v1/orders"], weights: [80, 20], thinkTime: 1, thresholds: ["http_req_failed rate < 1%", "http_req_duration p(95) < 500 ms"]}. Ramps and holds are seconds. Without a gate it aborts on its own at a 50% error rate or a 10 s p95.

scenario_id.description: Run this existing scenario (from telemetry_list_load_tests). A draft must be reviewed by the user first.

user_approved.description: true only after the user said yes to running this load now, against this target, at this load and for this long.

function.name: telemetry_search_logs
function.description: Search the production logs TaskTrooper Telemetry collected, newest first. Narrow by service, level and q or trace_id; an unfiltered week of logs is noise. Messages arrive with emails, IPs and keys masked, so a masked value is not a bug.

before.description: Cursor for older lines, the `nextBefore` of the previous page.

env.description: Deployment environment to read; omit for all.

level.description: An exact level, not a minimum. Query error and warn separately; the counts in the result show which levels have lines.

q.description: Full-text search. Use a term from the exception or span, not a whole sentence.

range.description: How far back to look; it must cover the incident.

route.description: A route template such as /orders/:id. It matches only lines that carry a route, so an empty answer means no routed lines, not no logs.

service.description: A service name as telemetry reports it.

trace_id.description: A 32-hex trace id. The most precise filter there is; try it first when you have a trace.

function.name: telemetry_search_traces
function.description: Search traces, or read one. For an error use errors_only, for latency use sort slowest with min_ms, keep the limit at 5 to 10, then open one or two representative traces by trace_id and find the failing or slow span, its dependency and its attributes (status, db statement, peer, exception).

endpoint.description: An endpoint in the form "METHOD /route" (for example "POST /v1/orders"), not the endpoint id slug. The wrong form returns an empty list, which is not the same as healthy.

env.description: Deployment environment to read; omit for all.

limit.description: Maximum traces, default 10, at most 100. Keep it small.

min_ms.description: Only traces at least this slow, in milliseconds.

range.description: How far back to look; it must cover the incident.

service.description: A service name as telemetry reports it.

sort.description: slowest for latency problems, recent otherwise.

trace_id.description: Read this one trace with all its spans (long traces are cut at the first spans). Give it alone; every other argument is then ignored.

function.name: telemetry_stop_load_test
function.description: Stop a queued or running load test at once. It needs no approval because it only takes load away: stop a run as soon as the target degrades beyond what the user agreed to, or when the user asks.

run_id.description: The run to stop, from telemetry_run_load_test or telemetry_list_load_tests.
